## TRA Timeline

#### IPO and TRA execution

- 2012-09-19: S-1/A Amendment No. 5 files the form-of TRA as Exhibit 10.25
- 2012-10-05: Berry IPO closes as a C-corp; board declares TRA rights as a dividend to record-date stockholders
- 2012-11-29: Executed Income Tax Receivable Agreement dated November 29, 2012
- 2012-12-17: 10-K files the executed TRA as Exhibit 10.25

#### Payment history and termination

- 2015-2018: Annual cash payments under the TRA ($39M, $57M, $111M, $37M across FY2015-FY2018)
- 2019-09-28 (FY2019 year-end): Berry negotiates a final settlement payment under the TRA's own Article IV early-termination mechanic, fully discharging the contract; total FY2019 payments $38M ($16M Q1, $22M Q4 final settlement)
- 2019-11-22: FY2019 10-K confirms termination

## Explanation

Berry Plastics (renamed Berry Global Group in 2017) IPO'd as a traditional C-corporation on October 5, 2012 and executed an Income Tax Receivable Agreement dated November 29, 2012 paying 85% of cash tax savings from utilization of pre-IPO net operating losses and AMT credit carryforwards to a beneficiary group of pre-IPO stockholders, option holders, and SAR holders, with Apollo Management Fund VI as Existing Stockholders Representative. Because Berry was a C-corp rather than Up-C, the TRA covered NOLs rather than basis step-ups. After roughly $282 million in cumulative payments from FY2015 through FY2018, Berry negotiated a final settlement payment in fiscal Q4 2019 that fully discharged the contract under the Article IV early-termination mechanic; no separate termination instrument was filed. Subsequent transactions (the 2024 Glatfelter spin-off and the April 2025 Amcor merger) had no further TRA effect. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
